Mention another volume only when it shares the same instance EBS baseline, and then as a Separate finding. Leave out AWS FIS experiments, AWS CloudTrail events and alarms on resources that are not attached to the instance.\\\\n- Link a gap only to the findings it affects. Each proposal also gives the exact AWS CLI command the customer can run with their own credentials. See [Change proposals](references/finding-logic.md#change-proposals).\\\\n- **Deletes are manual customer steps.** AWS DevOps Agent refuses delete-class operations (for example DeleteSnapshot, DeleteVolume, DeregisterImage), so never propose them as directed actions. State this rule in the answer whenever a modification is in progress or proposed.\\\\n- **No interpretation without data:** report what couldn\\'t be checked and use fallbacks. `DescribeVolumesModifications` returns only the most recent modification per volume; modification history and counts come from the optional AWS CloudTrail `ModifyVolume` events, or are listed under Gaps.\\\\n- **Units:** MiB/s for throughput, stated every time.\\\\n- **Escalate** on scope signals or when the investigation can\\'t explain the symptom.\\\\n\\\\n## Gotchas\\\\n\\\\n- A modification in `optimizing` is not stuck. The new size, IOPS or throughput already applies while it optimizes.\\\\n- `DescribeInstanceTypes` reports EBS bandwidth in MB/s. Convert it to MiB/s before comparing it with volume throughput.\\\\n- On io1 and io2, `VolumeThroughputPercentage` is the percentage of provisioned IOPS delivered. Troubleshoot paths use it when an operation failed on a limit.\\n\\n## Capacity and quota headroom\\n\\n**Checks**\\n\\nRun every check below even when the error looks simple. A user who reports a quota error has already failed to fix it alone, so give documented findings in the verdict format, not a short chat reply. Whether the run is a chat or a formal investigation is decided by how the user starts it, not by this skill.\\n\\n1. If an operation failed, quote the error and name the quota it refers to. For example \"You have exceeded your maximum io2 IOPS limit of 100000 IOPS in this region\" refers to the regional io2 IOPS quota, which is separate from the per-volume maximum.\\n2. `ListServiceQuotas --service-code ebs`: quota name, code, applied `Value`, `Adjustable`. Is the instance healthy and one volume flat at its own provisioned limit on the dimension its type is judged by, or is its `VolumeIOPSExceededCheck` or `VolumeThroughputExceededCheck` at 1?\\n   - Yes: **Volume**.\\n3. Are all layers below their limits, latency at the volume\\'s normal level, and queue length low?\\n   - Yes: **Not EBS**. Check CPU, memory, network and the application.\\n6.
